answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a quartz foundation for identity verification, requiring agents to bond assets to participate in consensus. By treating the network state as a mirror of economic commitment, the system ensures that spinning up identities is prohibitively expensive. An attacker seeking to infiltrate the orchard of decentralized nodes must incur massive capital expenditure, as each false identity requires proportional collateral, rendering large-scale Sybil attacks mathematically irrational.
